body:
Royalty revenue is collected on every chip shipped using Arm technology. In Q2 FY2026, royalty revenue reached a record $620 million, up 21% year over year. As customers adopt higher-value architectures such as Armv9 and Compute Subsystems, average royalty rates per chip increase.

Arm’s technology is organized across three business units announced at CES 2026: Cloud and AI, Edge (mobile and IoT), and Physical AI, which focuses on automotive and robotics.

Qualcomm's late-2025 acquisition of RISC-V leader Ventana Micro Systems signals growing institutional interest. However, Arm's mature software ecosystem, developer community (22M+ developers), and performance leadership create significant switching costs. Arm's DreamBig acquisition directly counters RISC-V's modularity advantage by offering chiplet-based [...] RISC-V disruption: The open-source RISC-V architecture poses a long-term competitive threat, particularly in cost-sensitive markets like IoT and edge computing. If Arm raises royalty rates too aggressively, it could accelerate customer migration.

title: Oregon’s chip industry risks becoming ‘insignificant’ globally, state report says - oregonlive.com
body:
By 

 Mike Rogoway | The Oregonian/OregonLive

Oregon’s semiconductor industry is in decline and is “at risk of becoming an insignificant stakeholder” globally, according to a new analysis commissioned by the state.

The report by Business Oregon, the state’s economic development agency, concludes the Silicon Forest faces “long-term stagnation” because it is too reliant on Intel, lacks homegrown talent and faces regulatory uncertainty, high costs and a diminished supply of industrial land. [...] The report warns that big semiconductor companies are investing in other states that have more aggressive economic development programs and do a better job preparing students for careers in technology. It suggests Oregon seek to nurture new, smaller semiconductor businesses to reduce its dependence on Intel and other legacy chip companies.
